text:
Jean-Gabriel Pageau has been a fixture in the Islanders' middle six for 460 games, the hometown Ottawa kid who became a Long Island regular after the 2020 trade. This season has been harder. He has 1 goal and 8 points in 17 games, and he has missed time since Nov. 12 with a lower-body injury. He left practice on Nov. 16, and coach Pete DeBoer said "fingers crossed" on Nov. 17 when asked if Pageau would be ready, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner.

The goal total is mostly bad luck. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, add up to 2.52, and he has scored on 4.5% of his shots, against a range our numbers put well above that. The rest of his game is the bigger question: at five-on-five, New York has had only about 44% of the chance quality with him on the ice, more than seven points worse than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with chances against piling up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still likes his puck work: 73% of his exits keep possession, and he carries the puck in on 56% of his entries.
headline: Jean-Gabriel Pageau is hurt and still waiting on goals
